knowledge:
- key_parameters: threshold=Determines the probe variation threshold in massi_select based on CV quantiles (1=All probes, 2=Upper 75%, 3=Upper 50%, 4=Upper 25%). Default is 3.
- alternatives: Using biomaRt to download genomic regions and Entrez gene IDs for probes and filtering for chromosome Y to obtain custom probe lists, which is recommended over manufacturer annotations because Ensembl maps probe sequences to reference genomes and allows removing ambiguous/non-specific probes.
- when_to_use: When analyzing public microarray datasets that lack associated sample sex information, or when needing to perform a sanity check to confirm sex information in gene expression datasets.
- pitfalls: The method is >97% accurate for datasets with 6 or more samples and with at least 15% of either males or females; outside this range, performance may be affected. A dip statistic < 0.08 from massi_dip suggests a potential sex bias (e.g., too few males or females) that could affect clustering accuracy, though it should be interpreted with caution. Low variance probes on the Y chromosome can be uninformative and should be filtered out using massi_select with an appropriate threshold.

workflows.name: microarray_dataframe_workflow
workflows.intent: Predict sample sex from a normalized microarray expression data.frame using Y chromosome probes.
input: expression_data.csv (normalized and log-transformed probe values with samples as columns and probes as rows)
y_probes.csv (Y chromosome probe identifiers as row names)
workflows.stages: 1. Extract Y chromosome probe data and calculate CV using massi_y ;; 2. Plot probe variation using massi_y_plot ;; 3. Select informative probes using massi_select ;; 4. Predict sample sex using massi_cluster ;; 5. Plot clustering results using massi_cluster_plot ;; 6. Check for sex bias using massi_dip
workflows.code:
massi.y.out <- massi_y(massi.test.dataset, massi.test.probes)
massi_y_plot(massi.y.out)
massi.select.out <- 
  massi_select(massi.test.dataset, massi.test.probes, threshold=4)
results <- massi_cluster(massi.select.out)
sample.results <- data.frame(results[[2]])
massi_cluster_plot(massi.select.out, results)
dip.result <- massi_dip(massi.select.out)

workflows.name: microarray_expressionset_workflow
workflows.intent: Predict sample sex from an ExpressionSet object and append the predicted sex back to the ExpressionSet phenoData.
input: expression_set.RData (ExpressionSet object containing normalized microarray data)
y_probes.csv (Y chromosome probe identifiers as row names)
workflows.stages: 1. Select Y chromosome probes from the ExpressionSet using massi_select ;; 2. Predict sample sex using massi_cluster ;; 3. Extract predicted sex results ;; 4. Match sample order and add results to the ExpressionSet phenoData
workflows.code:
eset.select.out <- 
  massi_select(massi.eset, massi.test.probes)

eset.results <- 
  massi_cluster(eset.select.out)

eset.sample.results <- 
  data.frame(eset.results[[2]])

sexData <- 
  data.frame(eset.sample.results[c("ID", "sex")])

eset.names <- 
  colnames(exprs(massi.eset))

sexData <- sexData[match(eset.names, sexData$ID),]

pData <- new("AnnotatedDataFrame", data = sexData)

phenoData(massi.eset) <- pData
